newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm but off highs.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm but off highs.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended firmer on Tuesday, but failed to break above a key resistance level due to a lack of fresh leads, dealers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract added 175 points to settle at 18,580 after opening on a positive note and trading to a high of 18,680.

Dealers said the dollar's firmer tone against the yen provided some support to the market, but attention would be increasingly focused on the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for February, due on Friday, for indications of the outlook for short-term interest rates.
"The chances of the market coming down are there, but there are no signals to tell me it's bearish," said a Japanese bank dealer. He said the March Nikkei should be supported around 18,400.
A dealer with a Japanese futures house said Tuesday's gains were merely the result of a technical rebound and would be capped below the 18,800 barrier.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 335.5 against its opening 333.0 on volume of 866 lots.
